Package org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic

Class AgenticToolCatalogParser

java.lang.Object
org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic.AgenticToolCatalogParser
public final class AgenticToolCatalogParser extends Object
Builds the tool catalogue of an agentic ad hoc sub process at parse time.

One AdHocToolDescriptor per directly startable child, in document order. Everything a turn needs to describe the child as a tool is read here, once, from the model — and everything that would make the child unusable as a tool refuses the deployment, instead of surfacing turns later as a runtime error the modeller never sees.

    • TOOL_CALL_READ

      protected static final Pattern TOOL_CALL_READ
      A read of one argument in an expression (CIB7-2136): toolCall.<name>, the name in group 1, or toolCall['<name>'], the name in group 2 or 3. A method of the map, such as toolCall.containsKey('x'), reads no argument of its name; a key computed in the brackets cannot be told at deployment. The name is the whole identifier, as EL reads it, so toolCall.betragé is no read of betrag.

    • refuseUndeclaredReadsInFollowers

      protected static void refuseUndeclaredReadsInFollowers(Element scopeElement, Collection<String> startableIds, Map<String,List<AdHocToolDescriptor.Parameter>> declared)
      Refuses a misspelt read of toolCall further along a tool's chain (CIB7-2136). An activity an inner flow reaches from a tool runs on the tool's performance, where the call's toolCall is visible; so do the flow's condition and the path of a boundary event on a tool or on such an activity. A flow into a throwing link event goes on from the catching one of its name, as the engine links them. A read there has to name a parameter that a tool whose flow reaches it declares in a mapping. No call's arguments arrive anywhere else in the scope, so a read of one there would read null, and is refused as well.
      Parameters:
      declared - the parameters of each tool, by the tool's id

    • resultVariables

      protected static List<String> resultVariables(AgenticToolCatalogParser.Parsing parsing, Element scopeElement, Element child, Map<String,String> properties)
      The process variables the child declares as its result.

      Derived rather than demanded: the model usually already says it. A child with output parameters, its own or those of a camunda:connector on it (an http call, an AI agent task, an agent in a nested ad hoc scope), declares exactly those: its outputs are what it hands out (CIB7-2239). A child without them declares camunda:resultVariable on the task and the ids of the camunda:formField entries a person fills in; a read-only field only shows a value and is no result. RESULT_VARIABLES_PROPERTY overrides them all — for a delegate calling setVariable directly, or to narrow what the agent is shown.

      A result variable or a form field a person fills in that the outputs do not hand out is then not shown to the agent, though the activity still writes it; a warning at deployment names it, so that the modeller hands it out or lists it on purpose.

    • readVariables

      protected static List<String> readVariables(Element child)
      The process variables the child reads, as far as its model says (CIB7-2169): the variable a simple expression of its input mapping names, or the root of a path, also of a camunda:connector on it; and the sources of a call activity's camunda:in. What a script, a delegate or a longer expression reads cannot be told from the model and is not listed. Left out are the call's own toolCall, and the names an expression gives itself, such as execution. Left out too is a name the activity's own input parameter creates, where the connector's inputs or camunda:in read it: they read the activity's execution, where that parameter is local. A multi-instance tool reads its collection, not its element variable and loop counters (multiInstanceReads(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.util.xml.Element, java.util.Set<java.lang.String>)).

    • blockedWhileOthersRun

      protected static boolean blockedWhileOthersRun(Element scopeElement, Element child, Map<String,String> properties)
      Whether the child carries BLOCKED_WHILE_OTHERS_RUN_PROPERTY.

      A value that is neither true nor false refuses the deployment. The runtime catalogue this replaces could only warn, because it read the property long after deployment; here the typo is caught where fixing it is cheap, and an activity meant to be guarded is never silently left unguarded.

    • parameters

      protected static List<AdHocToolDescriptor.Parameter> parameters(Element scopeElement, Element child, AgenticToolCatalogParser.Parsing parsing)
      The declared input parameters: the toolParameter(toolCall.<name>, ...) calls in the child's input mappings (CIB7-2136), and nothing else.

      Sorted by name, as the schema has always been: the same model keeps its schema, and moving an input mapping does not reorder it, so a prompt log's diff shows no noise.

    • storedWhole

      protected static Set<String> storedWhole(Element child)
      The parameters whose call is the whole value of one of the child's own input parameters, ${toolParameter(toolCall.<name>, ...)} and nothing around it: the input then holds the argument as it is (AdHocToolDescriptor.Parameter.isStoredWhole()). A list, a map or a script in the input, and a connector's inputs, which live only for the call, are left out.

    • refuseUndeclaredReadsInTool

      protected static void refuseUndeclaredReadsInTool(Element scopeElement, Element tool, Element element, Map<String,AdHocToolDescriptor.Parameter> byName)
      Refuses a read of toolCall.<name> anywhere in the tool that names no parameter it declares in a mapping (CIB7-2136): in its input mappings, where the declarations are, and as well in its output parameters, in the activities inside a sub process tool, in a call activity's mappings and in its conditions. A misspelt name would read null in each of them. Script code is no expression and is not read, but a script in JUEL is, and so are a script's attributes, a dynamic resource among them (reading(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.util.xml.Element)); the tools of an agent inside the tool are that agent's, and the connector inputs of an agent are judged by refuseInAgentConnector(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.util.xml.Element, org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.util.xml.Element, org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.util.xml.Element). A text that calls the function is left to the input mappings' own check above, or, anywhere else, to refuseUnreadCalls(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.util.xml.Element, java.util.Collection<java.lang.String>), which says the call declares nothing there.

    • addMappingDeclarations

      protected static void addMappingDeclarations(Element scopeElement, Element child, String text, Map<String,AdHocToolDescriptor.Parameter> byName, Set<String> typed)
      The parameters an input mapping declares with toolParameter(toolCall.<name>, '<description>', '<type>') (CIB7-2136); the description and the type may be left out, the type then being string. Only a call inside an expression counts, and only that form is read, with literals, so the schema is known at deployment; any other call of the function refuses the deployment, with the reason. A name may be used in several calls: a call without a type takes the type another one gives, two given types must agree, and so must two given descriptions: a call without one takes the one another gives.

      A parameter is required (CIB7-2135): it is listed in the schema's required array, and a call that leaves it out is refused before the activity starts. A trailing OPTIONAL_MARKER on the type marks it as one the model may leave out. A call without a type takes the marker with the type another call gives; two calls that give a type must agree on the marker too.

      Parameters:
      typed - the names whose type a call of this tool gave, so far

    • refuseUnreadCalls

      protected static void refuseUnreadCalls(Element scopeElement, Collection<String> startableIds)
      Refuses a call of the function the catalogue does not read (CIB7-2136). A tool parameter is declared only in an input parameter of an activity the agent starts, its own or its connector's; a call anywhere else in the scope would declare nothing, the model would never be offered the parameter, and the call would read null at run time. Script code is no expression, so a call there is refused as well. A tool that is itself an agent evaluates its connector's inputs on every turn of its own scope, not when it is started, and the catalogue reads no declaration there: a call or a read of toolCall there is refused, and its own input parameters are the place. The tools of a nested agent are left to that agent's own parse.

    • refuseCallsOutsideAgents

      public static void refuseCallsOutsideAgents(Element processElement)
      Refuses a call of the function that no agentic scope reads (CIB7-2136): anywhere outside an agentic ad hoc sub process, and in the own extension elements of an agentic scope that is no tool of another. The function is registered on every engine, so such a model would deploy, and the call would fail when it runs: nothing sets toolCall there. Inside an agentic scope the catalogue has judged every call already (refuseUnreadCalls(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.util.xml.Element, java.util.Collection<java.lang.String>)), so its children are left alone. So is a script here: no script engine knows the function, so a toolParameter( in a script that no agent starts is someone else's, a function of the script's own, say. The source of a dynamic script is an expression, though, and a call there is refused. So is a call in an attribute of the process itself, as its job priority, which the engine evaluates too.

    • refuseToolCallInOwnMappings

      protected static void refuseToolCallInOwnMappings(Element processElement, Element agent)
      Refuses a read of toolCall in the connector and in the own input and output parameters of an agentic scope that is no tool of another agent (CIB7-2136). The connector's inputs are read on every turn of the agent, the scope's inputs when it is entered and its outputs when it ends: no tool call's arguments arrive at any of them, so toolCall there would read null. An agent in or along a tool of another is judged by that agent's catalogue (refuseInAgentConnector(org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.util.xml.Element, org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.util.xml.Element, org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.util.xml.Element)); a call of the function there is refused before this, as anywhere outside a tool.
